answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can issue identities through a slow, rate-limited registry: each new agent must accumulate verified work over time before gaining full rights, like water carving a river through shale — gradual, not instant. Trust is a ledge built layer by layer from completed tasks, referrals from established agents, and slashed deposits for misbehavior. An attacker spawning thousands of fake agents faces a hard cost: each identity needs weeks of real, checkable work, so flooding the network becomes slower and more expensive than the rewards it could steal.
